source: Sep 9 Power Stack dossier + authoritative sources + MacroMicro cross-market verification
sourceStatus: MacroMicro was successfully accessed through current public series pages in this refresh. It is a supporting cross-market layer, not sole canonical proof. Fresher official data remains controlling where MacroMicro lags.
regime: Inflationary physical-capex expansion confronting a global duration shortage. Middle East product/shipping risk is re-accelerating inflation while Treasury/fiscal supply, AI-related debt and Japan monetary normalisation compete for long-duration capital. Physical AI/grid/power demand remains strong, but funding quality and cash conversion now matter as much as backlog growth.

channels.label: Growth / Demand
channels.regime: Nominal growth resilient, private demand uneven
channels.interpretation: US activity resists an immediate recession call while China private-credit demand remains weak and energy costs erode real purchasing power.

channels.label: Policy Relief
channels.interpretation: Oil/products, copper and strong services prices reduce central-bank room to offset tighter market-based conditions.

channels.label: Financial Conditions
channels.interpretation: MacroMicro confirms US10Y 4.79%, real10Y 2.42% and Japan10Y 2.89%. Treasury supply, AI debt and reduced Japanese duration suppression can keep clearing yields high even if policy rates stop rising.

channels.label: Weak-End Credit Stress
channels.interpretation: IG OAS remains tight at 0.81% and HY at 2.68%, but CCC OAS is 10.55%. Financing quality matters more than generic risk-on/risk-off labels.

channels.label: Consumer
channels.interpretation: Credit remains available but fuel and financing costs reduce future discretionary flexibility, supporting trade-down beneficiaries.

channels.label: Housing
channels.interpretation: Mortgage affordability remains hostage to the duration complex rather than only the Fed funds rate.

channels.label: Industrial / AI / Power Capex
channels.interpretation: Prefer funded backlog, signed PPAs, real interconnection work and existing generation over proposed capacity dependent on future financing.

channels.label: Input Costs
channels.interpretation: Oil/products, copper, electrical components, freight and cooling demand overlap, increasing the value of pricing power and pass-through.

channels.label: Risk Appetite
channels.interpretation: The S&P earnings yield of 3.79% sits about 1pp below the 4.79% US10Y, raising the valuation hurdle even without a confirmed broad bear market.

channels.label: Crude
channels.interpretation: Gulf disruption matters, but rerouting makes crude less convex than downstream products unless bypass infrastructure itself is hit.

channels.label: Refined Products
channels.interpretation: Diesel, jet and refining capacity are more dangerous for inflation than Brent alone; refiners and logistics gain relevance.

channels.label: US Gas / Global LNG
channels.interpretation: Gulf route risk and data-centre power growth reinforce contracted LNG and gas generation.

channels.label: Gold / Monetary Hedge
channels.regime: Structural support stronger, tactical real-yield headwind
channels.interpretation: China reserve accumulation and global duration/fiscal stress strengthen strategic gold, while 2.42% real yields keep entries rate-sensitive.

channels.label: Copper / Industrial Metals
channels.interpretation: Record copper confirms grid/AI scarcity, but China credit impulse 20.84 and negative July TSF RMB-loan growth argue against calling it broad domestic reflation.

channels.label: Battery Storage / Lithium
channels.interpretation: Peak-load stress improves storage/VPP economics while oversupply keeps the preference on integrators and deployment.

channels.label: Agriculture / Fertilizer Inputs
channels.interpretation: Energy/shipping shocks support fertilizer pricing but squeeze farm economics.

crossMarketWatch.interpretation: Not a broad credit panic. The stress is the price and availability of long-duration capital plus a weak-end credit tail.
chinaTransmission: TSF RMB-loan increase -CNY589.6bn in July MacroMicro series
crossMarketWatch.interpretationChina: Prefer state-backed infrastructure, exporters and verified orders over broad domestic-reflation beta.
